text: Bacillota_B gene-content expansion contrasts with Patescibacteria/CPR streamlining (≤1 Mbp, episymbiotic), but the cited Tian result concerns another superphylum. quote: This is the **opposite direction** from Tian et al. (2020)'s "small is mighty" Patescibacteria streamlining finding. Tian's claim was specific to the Patescibacteria/CPR superphylum (≤1 Mbp genomes, episymbiotic lifestyle). Within cultivable Bacillota_B (a different subsurface niche — anaerobic Firmicutes that grow free-living rather than as episymbionts), deep-clay specialization correlates with **gene-content expansion**, not reduction. This is consistent with Beaver & Neufeld (2024)'s "self-sufficiency" hypothesis and with Becraft et al. (2021)'s *Ca.* Desulforudis audaxviator (genome `GB_GCA_020725505.1` is in our anchor cohort) which Becraft showed retains a self-sufficient genome with full N-fixation + amino-acid biosynthesis + C-fixation — no streamlining.
